home.aboutTitle: A hand-kept catalogue of outdoor places across Taiwan
home.aboutBody: No live weather, surf reports or campsite availability here — others already do those well. This answers a different question: what is this place like, and does it suit me. Distance and ascent come from real tracks, and every duration says whether it was measured or estimated.
home.activitiesSub: Each activity has its own difficulty scale, because they are not comparable.

lead.hiking: Off the metro, on the ridge within ninety minutes.
lead.cycling: Riverside, then up. The tarmac never breaks.
lead.vtt: The pleasure isn't speed. It's reading the ground.
lead.climbing: The sea is underneath you, louder than the wind.
lead.camping: Dark arrives earlier than you planned for.
lead.surfing: It is only a break when the wind agrees.
lead.waterfall: By the time you hear it, you are still ten minutes out.
lead.diving: Underwater, Taiwan is a different island.

blurb.hiking: The trails across Yangmingshan and the city's edge are well signed and easy to plan alone. Each route here carries a measured distance and total ascent, and every duration is labelled — walked, or estimated.
blurb.cycling: Where the riverside path meets the mountain roads, gradient and surface change several times in one ride. Each route comes with its elevation profile, so you know what you are shifting into before you leave.
blurb.vtt: Forestry and farm tracks that change character with the rain. We record the line and the gradient; the surface is left to whoever rode it last, with the date attached.
blurb.climbing: Longdong's sandstone sea cliffs are Taiwan's principal natural crag. We record the location, the approach and where the route information came from — not grades, which belong to the crag's own consensus.
blurb.camping: Sites range from full hook-ups to nothing at all. What is recorded here is how you get there, the terrain and the elevation; pitches and fees belong to the site itself.
blurb.surfing: The north coast and the north-east each have their season and their wind. No live conditions here — that is well covered already — only what the spot is like and how you get in.
blurb.waterfall: The valleys around Pingxi and Sanxia hide falls of every size, most at the end of a trail. We record the walk in, the drop, and whether to go after rain.
blurb.diving: Green Island, Xiaoliuqiu, Kenting and the north-east coast all have places to get in, and depth, current and season differ sharply between them. Recorded here: where it is, how to reach it, and whether it is a shore or boat entry. Conditions and visibility belong to local reports on the day.

home.offerBody: Distance and ascent computed from a real track, a duration that says where it came from, and notes from someone who has been. Deciding whether a place suits you takes more than knowing where it is.

footer.blurb: A record of outdoor places across Taiwan — hiking, cycling, camping, surfing, diving, waterfalls, climbing and mountain biking. Still small, and growing one entry at a time.
